MEMORANDUM

TO: Engagement / Deal Team
FROM: International Trade & Sanctions Practice
DATE: August 10, 2026
RE: Counterparty Markup of CFIUS National Security Agreement — Risk-Prioritized Markup Analysis, Recommendations, and Counter-Draft Language

Confidential — Attorney Work Product / Privileged & Confidential

I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

We have reviewed the counterparty's markup of the draft CFIUS National Security Agreement ("NSA," the operative mitigation agreement) against the base materials, including the deal materials, the disclosure schedules and exhibits (Schedule 3.7, Schedule 5.2, and Exhibit B), and the controlling deal-team correspondence. The counterparty accepts most firm-standard and market-standard provisions, but its latest markup introduces three material deviations that must be reconciled against the base documents:

1. Indemnification cap reduction and conversion of the indemnity basket from a deductible to a tipping basket;
2. New Material Adverse Effect ("MAE") carve-outs for regulatory action of precisely the kind at issue in this matter; and
3. A shortened limitation period (survival) for the core representations.

Pursuant to the controlling partner instruction (the latest message in the deal-team email thread, which supersedes all earlier priorities), the client will concede the basket conversion but treats any survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue. Our recommendations below are risk-prioritized and reflect that controlling instruction. We also reconcile the counterparty's changes against the disclosure schedules, which control over general statements in the base materials.

Recommendation Summary (highest risk first):
- Item 3 (Survival-period reduction): REJECT — walk-away issue. Restore Exhibit B survival matrix.
- Item 2 (MAE carve-outs for regulatory action): REJECT — carve-outs intersect two pending regulatory inquiries disclosed in Schedule 3.7 and would gut NSA protections.
- Item 1 (Indemnification cap reduction; basket conversion): Basket conversion — CONCEDE per instruction. Cap reduction — push back; preserve cap and prevent silent shifting of Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities onto the client.

II. BACKGROUND AND BASIS OF REVIEW

A. Governing Instrument. This engagement concerns a CFIUS National Security Agreement (mitigation agreement) entered into to address U.S. Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States ("CFIUS") national security concerns arising from a covered transaction. The NSA contains representations and warranties, affirmative and negative covenants, conditions, indemnification, and termination provisions.

B. Sources Reviewed. We reconciled the counterparty markup against the following:
- Draft NSA (base deal materials);
- Counterparty markup (which identifies the deviations);
- Disclosure Schedule 3.7 (disclosing two pending regulatory inquiries intersecting the MAE carve-outs);
- Disclosure Schedule 5.2 (retained liabilities affected by the indemnification changes);
- Exhibit B (the survival matrix controlling the limitation periods); and
- Deal-team correspondence (whose controlling final message revises the negotiation priorities).

C. Governing Instruction. The deal-team correspondence states that the latest message REVISES the analysis priorities: the client will concede the basket conversion but treats any survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue. Earlier messages stating the opposite priority ordering are superseded and do not control. This memo implements the controlling instruction.

III. RISK-PRIORITIZED ANALYSIS OF MATERIAL CHANGES

RISK LEVEL: HIGH — Item 3: Limitation Period / Survival of Core Representations

A. The Change. The counterparty's markup shortens the survival period for the core representations, substituting a new limitation period that materially limits the window in which the client may assert claims for breach of fundamental representations and warranties.

B. Reconciliation Against Base Materials. Exhibit B to the NSA establishes the survival matrix controlling the limitation periods for the various representations and warranties. The counterparty's markup contradicts Exhibit B by shortening the survival of the core representations. Under Schedule/exhibit priority rules, the scheduled exceptions and operating schedule control over general statements in the base materials. Because Exhibit B sets the definitive survival matrix, the markup's limitation-period change is unsupported and contravenes the negotiated schedule.

C. Risk Assessment. This change carries the highest risk in the markup because:
- It directly reduces the client's ability to assert claims for the most important representations (e.g., authority, ownership, and the fundamental national-security/CFIUS-compliance representations).
- In the CFIUS NSA context, a shortened survival window could prematurely extinguish the client's rights to enforce mitigation commitments and to seek recourse for breach.
- The controlling partner instruction identifies this as a WALK-AWAY issue. We should treat the survival-period reduction as non-negotiable in any commercially reasonable posture.

D. Recommendation. REJECT the survival-period reduction. Restore the survival matrix set forth in Exhibit B. Given the controlling instruction elevating this to a walk-away matter, no concession on this point is authorized.

E. Counter-Draft Language.
Base (restore): "The representations and warranties of the Parties set forth in this NSA shall survive the execution and delivery of this NSA and the Closing indefinitely, and in any event for the survival periods set forth in Exhibit B. No such representation or warranty shall expire or be limited by any shorter limitation of action or survival provision, and nothing in Section [X] (Limitation Periods) shall shorten the survival of the core representations and warranties set forth in Exhibit B."

Rejecting language (markup): Delete the counterparty's insertion that reads substantially as follows, and any analogous shortened limitation language — "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary herein, all representations and warranties shall terminate on the date that is [X] months following the Closing" — and replace with the restored survival matrix of Exhibit B.

RISK LEVEL: HIGH — Item 2: MAE Definition — New Carve-Outs for Regulatory Action

A. The Change. The counterparty's markup amends the definition of "Material Adverse Effect" to add carve-outs excluding regulatory action of the kind at issue in this matter.

B. Reconciliation Against Base Materials. Disclosure Schedule 3.7 identifies two pending regulatory inquiries that directly intersect the very regulatory-action carve-outs the counterparty seeks to add. Under the schedule/exhibit priority rules, Schedule 3.7 (a scheduled exception controlling over general statements) confirms these inquiries are live and material at signing. Adding a carve-out for "regulatory action" of this kind would carve the disclosed inquiries out of the MAE definition and, in a CFIUS mitigation context, would undermine the client's ability to invoke MAE-based protections or enforce conditions premised on a continuing absence of adverse regulatory action.

C. Risk Assessment. This change is a material deviation because:
- It neuters the MAE definition precisely where the disclosed pending regulatory inquiries live, effectively shifting the risk of regulatory action (the central risk of this CFIUS engagement) onto the client.
- In an NSA/mitigation-agreement context, regulatory-action carve-outs of this kind are contrary to the protective intent of the instrument and to market practice for national-security mitigation documents.
- Because Schedule 3.7 already discloses the two inquiries, the carve-out is not a neutral market accommodation; it is targeted at the exact exposures that are the subject of this matter.

D. Recommendation. REJECT the MAE carve-outs, at least as drafted. At a minimum, redraft the carve-outs so that they do not exclude (i) the two pending regulatory inquiries disclosed in Schedule 3.7, or (ii) regulatory action that would constitute a violation of the NSA's mitigation covenants or would give rise to a national-security concern under the CFIUS order/mitigation framework. Preserve the client's right to treat the consummation or outcome of such inquiries as a Material Adverse Effect.

E. Counter-Draft Language.
Base (rejecting): "For the avoidance of doubt, 'Material Adverse Effect' shall not be deemed to exclude, and the carve-outs in this definition shall not apply to, any Effect arising out of or relating to any pending, threatened, or anticipated investigation, inquiry, subpoena, or regulatory action of a Governmental Authority that is disclosed in Schedule 3.7 or that would constitute or reasonably be expected to result in a breach of this NSA, including the mitigation covenants set forth in Sections [X] through [Y], or that is otherwise attributable to the covered transaction or its review by CFIUS."

Rejecting language (markup): Strike the counterparty's new carve-out for "any government or regulatory action, investigation, inquiry or proceeding, including any action by CFIUS or any U.S. regulatory authority," and the consequential amendment to the definition of MAE, and replace with the redraft above and restore the original MAE definition.

RISK LEVEL: MODERATE — Item 1: Indemnification Cap Reduction and Basket Conversion

A. The Change. The counterparty's markup (i) silently reduces the aggregate indemnification cap and (ii) converts the indemnity basket from a deductible to a tipping basket.

B. Reconciliation Against Base Materials. Disclosure Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities that the indemnification changes would silently shift. By reducing the cap and switching to a tipping basket, the markup increases the client's exposure and shifts responsibility for retained liabilities onto the client without a corresponding adjustment in consideration or disclosure.

C. Negotiation Instruction. The controlling partner instruction directs that the client WILL CONCEDE the basket conversion. Accordingly, we treat the conversion from a deductible to a tipping basket as a conceded point and do not object to it. However, the concession is limited to the basket conversion and does not extend to the separate, silent reduction of the aggregate cap.

D. Recommendation. (i) Concede the basket conversion as directed. (ii) Push back on the separate cap reduction: do not accept any reduction in the aggregate indemnification cap absent a corresponding adjustment (e.g., an increase in purchase price/consideration or a broadening of the retained-liability provisions). Ensure Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities remain the responsibility of the counterparty rather than being silently shifted to the client through the cap reduction.

E. Counter-Draft Language.
Basket (concede): "The indemnification obligations of the Parties shall be subject to an aggregate basket equal to [●]; once such aggregate amount is exceeded, the indemnifying Party shall be responsible for all Losses from the first dollar (a 'tipping basket'), consistent with the parties' agreement to convert the prior deductible to a tipping basket."

Cap (reject/preserve): "Notwithstanding the foregoing, the aggregate limit of the indemnifying Party's liability under this NSA shall be [●] and shall not be reduced by the markup; for the avoidance of doubt, the Parties confirm that (i) the retained liabilities listed on Schedule 5.2 remain the sole responsibility of the counterparty and (ii) no change to the indemnification cap or to the retention schedule shall have the effect of shifting such retained liabilities to the client."

Rejecting language (markup): Strike the counterparty's reduced-cap figure and any corresponding reallocation of Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities, and insert the preserved-cap language above.

IV. RECONCILIATION OF SCHEDULES AND EXHIBITS

Consistent with the schedule/exhibit priority rule, the scheduled exceptions and exhibits control over general statements in the base materials:
- Schedule 3.7 (two pending regulatory inquiries) controls the analysis of the MAE carve-outs and confirms their materiality.
- Schedule 5.2 (retained liabilities) controls the analysis of the indemnification changes and confirms their exposure-shifting effect.
- Exhibit B (survival matrix) controls the limitation-period analysis and is contradicted by the markup's survival reduction.
Each deviation in the counterparty markup has been reconciled against these controlling schedules above.

V. CONCLUSION AND NEXT STEPS

We recommend a risk-prioritized negotiation posture: (1) reject the survival-period reduction (walk-away issue, restore Exhibit B); (2) reject the MAE carve-outs for regulatory action, reconciled against Schedule 3.7; and (3) concede the basket conversion per instruction while preserving the indemnification cap and the Schedule 5.2 retained-liability allocation. Counter-draft language for each material change is set forth above and should be incorporated into the next iteration of the NSA. We recommend the deal team NOT accept the survival reduction under any circumstances given the controlling instruction, and to hold firm on the MAE carve-outs given the disclosed regulatory inquiries.

Please contact the undersigned with any questions.

[END OF MEMORANDUM]
